text:
Alex W: FYI we saw a p99 tail spike yesterday during a customer burst — several SLO violation alerts between 03:12-03:14 UTC. Dumping profiling/data here.
Maria S: saw the alerts. attaching short summary from the profiler: p50=45ms, p95=210ms, p99=880ms for /v1/generate on rtx-dedicated pool. trace ids: trace-9f2a, trace-9f2b.
Alex W: key observations: (1) KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 68% during the burst; (2) many requests opted into kernel fallback path — fallback kernel avg token time ~3.2ms vs primary ~0.9ms; (3) autoscale added 2 GPUs but only after ~38s.
Kenji T: raw flamegraph attached (pasted subset):
```
cpu 50%  kernel_fallback_execute
cpu 30%  attention_kernels::matmul
cpu 10%  kv_cache::populate
```
Kenji T: The fallback was triggered because the runtime saw sequence length variance > 1.2x and switched to the generic kernel. Our current kernel-selector threshold is aggressive for mixed-length microbatches.
Maria S: batching telemetry: during burst microbatch sizes increased to 120-140 (we cap at 160). Queueing delay median jumped from 6ms -> 120ms while waiting for microbatch to fill. That explains p95 inflation.
Dana P: autoscaler logs? ops-bot:
ops-bot: [03:12:22] scale_request -> +2 gpus
ops-bot: [03:13:00] pod_ready -> gpu-17
ops-bot: [03:13:00] pod_ready -> gpu-18
ops-bot: note: init container prewarm job required GPUs to start model weights; KV warming only begins after pod readiness.
Alex W: so three contributors: KV cold misses, larger microbatches creating queueing, and kernel fallback multiplier. All amplify tail.
Kenji T: proposed short-term mitigations:
- reduce microbatch max for latency-tier routes from 160 -> 64
- make kernel-selector prefer fast kernel when seq_len < 512 even if variance slightly > threshold (tweak threshold from 1.2 -> 1.5 for short seqs)
- add lightweight KV prewarm: on scale-up fire N synthetic requests with short prefixes to populate KV for the active model shard
Maria S: I ran a sim locally: apply microbatch cap 64 + KV prewarm (10 synthetic reqs per new pod) -> p99 drops from 880ms -> ~260ms in load replay. cost delta: ~+3% traffic tokens billed due to prewarm.
Dana P: long-term: could we change autoscaler to pre-create warm standby with only weights loaded and KV warmed? costy but nice. Also consider faster kernel compile path to avoid fallback during bursts.
Kenji T: agree. A/B plan: start with microbatch cap change + prewarm on canary pool for VIP customers for 48h. If p99 < 350ms and no regressions, roll to main pool.
Alex W: action items:
- Kenji: PR to change microbatch cap + kernel-selector tweak (target: 24h)
- Maria: implement KV prewarm hook in scaleup sequence + synthetic job (target: 48h)
- Dana: estimate cost delta for standby-warm strategy and run licensing/cost review (target: EOW)
- Ops: add alert that correlates autoscale latency (scale request -> pod ready) with p99 SLO breaches (Ops/Infra)
Maria S: quick note: need to watch for quality regressions from prewarm synthetic prompts — we'll use simple neutral prefix so model weights/KV keys are representative.
Alex W: thanks. tagging @eng-oncall to monitor tonight's traffic. :thumbsup:
